SMTO-EXE-0170 — SMTO couldn't find the document

GUID: 41f7f4f8-1c81-5092-895a-dbcc17a99c4a
Slug: office-file-not-found
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO looked for the file on the computer it's working on, but the file isn't there under that name and folder. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the file's exact name, including its ending such as .docx, .xlsx or .pptx, and the folder it's in. A small difference in the name or folder means SMTO looks in the wrong place.
  2. Make sure the file is on the computer running the selected Gateway. Check the conversation's Target menu to see which computer that is. SMTO searches that computer, which may not be the device you're typing on.
  3. If the file is on your own device, attach it with Add context and ask SMTO to use the attached file. Attached files are copied to the right computer for SMTO to open.
  4. Ask SMTO again with the full folder path and file name. Nothing was changed the first time, so it's safe to try again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the document and shows its contents or makes your change.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the full file location, to the person who manages the Gateway computer. The file may have been moved, renamed or deleted there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Office operation on the selected Gateway raised file-not-found (FileNotFoundError or File not_found) for the requested path, so nothing was read or written (office.file_not_found).

What this means

  • Office processing caught FileNotFoundError or a File not-found condition while accessing the requested local resource. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Office processing caught FileNotFoundError or a File not-found condition while accessing the requested local resource.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exact missing source or auxiliary input from the request and retained phase; avoid searching another Gateway implicitly.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the exact path exists on the selected Gateway (relative paths resolve against the execution working directory there; there is no controller fallback). Transfer the file to that Gateway or attach it as authorized context, then retry with the exact target-local path.
  • Find or transfer the file to the selected Gateway, then use its exact target-local path.

Retry and execution caution

  • Find or transfer the file to the selected Gateway, then use its exact target-local path.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended accessible local file exists before the document operation proceeds.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
